payload.body:
Implemented at 79894db.

The site (fleet/run-engine.mjs, the setup-commit staging scan) now runs `git status --porcelain -uall` and filters out any path carrying a `node_modules` segment before the `bootstrapManifestChanged([p])` basename test.

Two decisions a later session would otherwise rediscover:

1. The node_modules exclusion is a SEGMENT test (`p.split("/").includes("node_modules")`), not a prefix test, and it lives at this scan — not inside `bootstrapManifestChanged`. That helper is also read by the pre-review manifest scan and by the lockfile-regeneration gates, and those readings want a vendored `package.json` to still count as a manifest change; only the staging scan wants it excluded.

2. Measured in a scratch repo (2026-09-17) with `client/package.json` and `node_modules/left-pad/package.json` untracked and the root `package.json` modified: default porcelain prints ` M package.json`, `?? client/`, `?? node_modules/`; `-uall` prints ` M package.json`, `?? client/package.json`, `?? node_modules/left-pad/package.json`. So the filtered, sorted set is exactly `client/package.json`, `package.json` — M1 — with nothing under `node_modules/` — M2.

`fleet/CONTRACT.md`'s setup-commit sentence names `-uall` and keeps the `node_modules/` clause as a stated exclusion (M4).

The existing S1 leg (c2) is untouched: the sim as it stands at BASE still prints ALL TESTS PASSED, so a run whose add line writes only `bun.lock` and the root `package.json` makes the same setup commit it made at BASE (M3). The new nested scenario is the peer exam's to write; I wrote no test file.

payload.body:
examiner (exam round 1): approach for the exam at fleet/tests/test_run_engine_ready_set.mjs.

Adding one section at the foot of the sim, grouped under a comment naming Task 2 and #1097, leaving every existing leg untouched. It drives ONE new red-baseline scenario (tag 'rb') and reads the existing 'e2' run back out of RUNS.

Legs as the Proof states them:
 (a) [M1] the new run's check.sh prints the four FAILED lines in the Proof's order (beta, other, alpha, beta) and exits 1; assert exactly one TEST_FAILED waveMerges row, its detail contains 'failing: fleet/tests/test_beta.mjs, tests/test_other.py, fleet/tests/test_alpha.mjs (', the red-baseline judgment call contains the same substring, and neither carries 'tests/test_fleet_suite.py'.
 (b) [M2] the existing e2 run (check.sh prints nothing) parks with a detail containing 'failing: unparsed ('.
 (c) [M3] both runs' TEST_FAILED detail and both red-baseline judgment calls startWith the exact head 'baseline: the suite is RED on BASE — the sensor is blind for this run; failing: ', and e2's detail still matches /inherited that red/.

Reading of leg (a) that a later session would otherwise have to reconstruct: the four FAILED lines are printed UNDER a pytest-shaped preamble ('=== FAILURES ===', a '___ test_fleet_mjs[test_beta.mjs] ___' header, an 'E   AssertionError' line, '=== short test summary info ==='). That is forced by the leg's own last clause. The detail is redBaselineHead(baseline.output) and baseline.output is failingBlock(raw); failingBlock's START matches '^FAILED ', so a check.sh printing bare FAILED lines puts all four INSIDE the quoted block and the detail then carries 'tests/test_fleet_suite.py' no matter what the reading does — the clause would be unsatisfiable. With the real pytest shape the block is cut at the '=== short test summary info ===' line (END is '^={3,} '), which is exactly what run-engine.mjs's own comment at line 2896 says ('the short summary … is BELOW the block failingBlock cuts'), so the FAILED lines reach failingTestPaths via the RAW stdout+stderr and never reach the quotation. The Proof's 'prints, in this order, <four lines>, then exits 1' is satisfied: those four lines are printed in that order.

payload.body:
Task 2 done in one edit: the local `failingPaths(raw)` at fleet/run-engine.mjs:2901 now reads through the exported `failingTestPaths` (line 105) instead of its own `/^FAILED (.+?)::/` map — translation of bridge lines to `fleet/tests/<name>.mjs`, dedup, first-seen order, no sort. Empty list still renders `unparsed` (M2). `redBaselineHead` and both its readers (judgment call, parkOnRedBaseline detail) are untouched, so M3's head is byte-identical.

Verified directly: failingTestPaths on the leg (a) fixture returns `fleet/tests/test_beta.mjs, tests/test_other.py, fleet/tests/test_alpha.mjs`, and on '' returns [] -> 'unparsed'.

One note for whoever writes/reads the exam. Leg (a)'s final clause — 'neither detail nor call contains tests/test_fleet_suite.py at all' — is fixture-dependent, not implementation-dependent. The head ends with ` (` + baseline.output + `)`, and for a red baseline baseline.output is failingBlock(stdout+stderr). failingBlock's START is /^(___ .+ ___$|FAILED |FAIL[: ]|not ok |AssertionError)/ and its END does not match a FAILED line, so a check.sh that prints ONLY the four FAILED lines has its whole output quoted back inside the parens — bridge path and all. Real pytest puts the FAILED short-summary BELOW the block (the comment at line 2896 says exactly this), so on real output the clause holds. If the exam's check.sh emits the four bare FAILED lines, that clause fails on ANY implementation that keeps the block where M3 says it has always been; if it emits pytest-shaped output (=== FAILURES ===, ___ header ___, E lines, === short test summary info ===, FAILED ...), the block is the first failure's block and the clause holds. Implemented as written rather than rewriting the quoted block, which nothing asked for.
